'''Sir Tejinder Singh Virdee''', {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}} ([[Punjabi language|Punjabi]]: ਤਜਿੰਦਰ ਸਿੰਘ ਵਿਰਦੀ, born 13 October 1952), is a [[Kenya]]n-born British [[Experimental physics|experimental particle physicist]] and Professor of Physics at [[Imperial College London]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Imperial College Reference|url=http://www3.imperial.ac.uk/people/t.virdee}}</ref> He is best known for originating the concept of the [[Compact Muon Solenoid]] (CMS) alongside a few other colleagues and has been referred to as one of the 'founding fathers' <ref>{{cite news|title=CERN Courier Article: Inside story: the search in CMS for the Higgs boson|url=http://cerncourier.com/cws/article/cern/50566|access-date=7 December 2012|newspaper=CERN Courier|archive-date=25 November 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121125071524/http://cerncourier.com/cws/article/cern/50566|url-status=dead}}</ref> of the project. CMS is a world-wide collaboration which started in 1991 and now has over 3500 participants from 50 countries.

In recognition of his work on CMS, Virdee has been awarded numerous prizes and distinctions. In 2007, he was awarded the IOP High Energy Particle Physics group prize<ref name="2007 HEPP Prize">{{cite web|title=2007 HEPP Prize|url=http://www.iop.org/activity/groups/subject/hepp/prize/group/page_40779.html|access-date=7 December 2012}}</ref> and in 2009 the IOP [[Chadwick Medal and Prize]].<ref name="IOP: 2009 Chadwick Medal citation">{{cite web|title=Chadwick Medal|url=http://www.iop.org/about/awards/subject/chadwick/medallists/page_38531.html}}</ref> In 2012 he was elected Fellow of the [[Royal Society]]<ref name="Fellow of the Royal Society">{{cite web|title=Fellow of the Royal Society|url=http://royalsociety.org/people/tejinder-virdee/}}</ref> and Honorary Fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]] (IOP).<ref>{{cite web |title=Honorary Fellows: Professor Sir Tejinder Singh Virdee |url=https://www.iop.org/about/awards/honorary-fellowship/our-honorary-fellows/professor-sir-tejinder-singh-virdee |website=Institute of Physics |access-date=16 January 2025}}</ref> In 2013 he was awarded the [[Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics|Special Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics]] for "leadership in the scientific endeavour that led to the discovery of the new Higgs-like particle by the [[ATLAS experiment|ATLAS]] and CMS collaborations at [[CERN]]'s [[Large Hadron Collider]] (LHC)",<ref name="2012 Special Fundamental Physics Prize">{{cite web|title=2012 Special Fundamental Physics Prize|url=http://www.fundamentalphysicsprize.org/laureates/laureates2|access-date=11 December 2012|archive-date=14 December 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121214063312/http://www.fundamentalphysicsprize.org/laureates/laureates2|url-status=dead}}<p>Virdee plans to use the money to support science in schools in Sub-Saharan Africa—see {{Cite web|author=Peter Woit|author-link=Peter Woit|date=12 June 2013|title=Nature on the new Nobels|url=http://www.math.columbia.edu/~woit/wordpress/?p=6021|publisher=Not Even Wrong|access-date=22 June 2013}}</p></ref>  and the [[European Physical Society]] [[High Energy and Particle Physics Prize]].<ref name="2013 European Physical Society High Energy Physics Prize">{{cite web|title=High Energy Particle Physics Prize|url=https://eps-hepp.web.cern.ch/hepp-prize-awards.php|access-date=7 February 2026|archive-date=|archive-url=|url-status=|last=High Energy Particle Physics Division of EPS}}</ref>

In 2015 he was awarded the IOP Glazebrook Medal and Prize for his leadership of the Compact Muon Solenoid (CMS) experiment at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) where evidence for the Higgs boson was revealed after 20 years of research involving design, construction and data-taking. In 2017 he was granted the [[American Physical Society]] [[Panofsky Prize]] for his pioneering work and outstanding leadership in the making of the CMS experiment,<ref>{{cite web|title=W.K.H. Panofsky Prize in Experimental Particle Physics|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/panofsky.cfm|website=APS Physics|access-date=5 January 2017}}</ref> and in 2020 the Blaise Pascal Medal of the European Academy of Sciences in Physics.<ref name="European Academy of Sciences">{{cite web |title=EURASC Awardees - Blaise Pascal Medals |url=https://www.eurasc.org/eurasc-awardees/blaise-pascal-medals |website=European Academy of Sciences |access-date=11 June 2020}}</ref> In 2024, he was awarded the Royal Medal (Physical) of the Royal Society.<ref>{{cite web |title=Royal Medals 2024 |url=https://royalsociety.org/medals-and-prizes/royal-medals/ |website=Royal Society |access-date=16 January 2025}}</ref> The citation reads: "for extraordinary leadership and profound impact on all phases of the monumental CMS experiment at the CERN Large Hadron Collider, including the crucial discovery of the Higgs boson through its decays to two photons."

In 2014, Virdee was knighted in the Queen's Birthday Honours list for services to science.<ref name=Knighthood>{{cite web|title=Knighthood|url=https://www.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/319884/Birthday_Honours_FCO_Notes_on_higher_awards.pdf|publisher=British Government|access-date=12 July 2014}}</ref>

Virdee has served on Scientific Advisory Committees of numerous international physics institutes and on the Physical Sciences jury for the [[Infosys Prize]] in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Infosys Prize - Jury 2020|url=http://www.infosys-science-foundation.com/prize/jury/jury-2020.asp|access-date=2020-12-10|website=www.infosys-science-foundation.com}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Tejinder Virdee was born in 1952 to Sikh parents Udham Kaur and Chain Singh Virdee in [[Nyeri]], [[Kenya]]. Virdee went to school in Kisumu at the Kisumu Boys High School. Due to the prevailing [[Indians in Kenya|circumstances]] in Kenya at the time, his family (of Indian [[Sikh]] origin) emigrated in 1967 to [[Birmingham]], England.<ref name="BBC World Service: Life Scientific">{{cite web|title=BBC World Service: Life Scientific|url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/radio/player/p00s5p5b}}{{dead link|date=September 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> He credits part of his interest in physics to Howard Stockley, his physics teacher at [[King's Norton Boys' School]], Birmingham, whom he describes as an 'inspirational teacher'.<ref name="BBC World Service: Life Scientific"/> He also remembers visiting [[Birmingham Museum of Science and Industry]], where he stumbled across a cloud chamber sparking his interest in the study of the structure of matter. Virdee obtained a B.Sc. in Physics from [[Queen Mary College, University of London]] in 1974.

==Research career==
After completing his Ph.D. at [[Imperial College London]], on an experiment conducted at the Stanford Linear Accelerator Center ([[SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory|SLAC]]) in [[California]],<ref>{{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.476103|uk.bl.ethos.476103}}</ref> he joined [[CERN]] in 1979 as a Fellow of the Experimental Physics Division. Virdee’s early scientific career (1979-1984) involved verifying the strange notion that the “quarks” (the constituents of the protons the neutrons and all other hadrons) carry fractional electric charge. This was successfully demonstrated by the NA14 photoproduction experiment at [[CERN]] in the mid-eighties.<ref name="Measurement of deep inelastic Compton scattering of high energy photons">{{cite journal|last=Astbury|first=P.|title=Measurement of deep inelastic Compton scattering of high energy photons|journal=Physics Letters B|date=1 March 1985|volume=152|issue=5–6|pages=419–427|doi=10.1016/0370-2693(85)90521-0|display-authors=etal|bibcode=1985PhLB..152..419A|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/157032}}</ref> Following NA14 he joined the [[UA1 experiment|UA1]] experiment at [[CERN]]'s proton-antiproton collider ([[Super Proton Synchrotron|SPS]]) where his interest in high-performance calorimetry was developed, leading to his invention of a novel technique of collecting light in plastic scintillator-based calorimeters.<ref name="A uranium scintillator calorimeter with plastic-fibre readout">{{cite journal|last=Albrow|first=M.G. |author2=Arnison, G. |author3=Bunn, J. |author4=Clarke, D. |author5=Cochet, C. |author6=Colas, P. |author7=Dallman, D. |author8=de Brion, J.P. |author9=Denby, B. |author10=Eisenhandler, E. |author11=Garvey, J. |author12=Grayer, G. |author13=Hill, D. |author14=Krammer, M. |author15=Locci, E. |author16=Pigot, C. |author17=Robinson, D. |author18=Siotis, I. |author19=Sobie, R. |author20=Szoncso, F. |author21=Verrecchia, P. |author22=Virdee, T.S. |author23=Wahl, H.D. |author24=Wildish, A. |author25=Wulz, C.-E. |title=A uranium scintillator calorimeter with plastic-fibre readout|journal=Nuclear Instruments and Methods in Physics Research Section A: Accelerators, Spectrometers, Detectors and Associated Equipment|date=31 March 1987|volume=256|issue=1|pages=23–37|doi=10.1016/0168-9002(87)91035-7|bibcode=1987NIMPA.256...23A|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/171434 }}</ref>

Towards the end of [[UA1 experiment|UA1]], (1990) Virdee, with a few other colleagues, started planning an experiment based on a high field solenoid that would be able to identify the missing elements of the [[Standard Model]] (SM) and also to probe in full the physics of the TeV scale. This was to become the [[Compact Muon Solenoid|CMS]] experiment at the [[Large Hadron Collider|LHC]],<ref name="CMS Letter of Intent">{{cite web|title=CMS Letter of Intent|url=http://cmsdoc.cern.ch/LoI/Authors.html|access-date=7 December 2012}}</ref> one of the most complex instruments science has ever seen. Since 1991 Virdee has played a crucial role in all phases of [[Compact Muon Solenoid|CMS]]. Over the last two decades this has covered conceptual design, intensive R&D, prototyping, construction, installation, commissioning, data-taking and finally physics exploitation. He has been the driving force behind many of the major technology decisions made in [[Compact Muon Solenoid|CMS]], especially the selection of the calorimeter technologies. The [[Compact Muon Solenoid|CMS]] hadron calorimeter uses the technique he had invented earlier.<ref name="A uranium scintillator calorimeter with plastic-fibre readout" />

The possibility of discovering a Higgs-like boson played a crucial role in the conceptual design of [[Compact Muon Solenoid|CMS]],<ref name="Experimental Challenges in High-Luminosity Collider Physics">{{cite journal|last=Ellis|first=N|author2=Virdee, T S |title=Experimental Challenges in High-Luminosity Collider Physics|journal=[[Annual Review of Nuclear and Particle Science]]|date=1 December 1994|volume=44|issue=1|pages=609–653|doi=10.1146/annurev.ns.44.120194.003141| doi-access=free |bibcode=1994ARNPS..44..609E}}</ref><ref name="Physics requirements for the design of the ATLAS and CMS experiments at the Large Hadron Collider">{{cite journal|last=Virdee|first=T. S.|title=Physics requirements for the design of the ATLAS and CMS experiments at the Large Hadron Collider|journal=Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A: Mathematical, Physical and Engineering Sciences|date=16 January 2012|volume=370|issue=1961|pages=876–891|doi=10.1098/rsta.2011.0459|pmid=22253241|bibcode=2012RSPTA.370..876V|doi-access=free}}</ref>  and served as a benchmark to test the performance of the experiment. In 1992, at a meeting in Evian,<ref>{{cite web |author1=CERN |title=Early days: The Evian experiment meeting |url=https://cerncourier.com/a/early-days-the-evian-experiment-meeting-archive/ |website=CERN Courier |date=19 September 2008 |access-date=29 August 2024}}</ref> entitled ‘Towards the LHC Experimental Programme’ meeting, Virdee championed the case for the selection of CMS amongst four competing experiment conceptual designs. After much deliberation, CERN’s LHC experiments peer-review committee, the LHCC, eventually chose two, one being the CMS design. 
In 1990 Virdee and a colleague, Christopher Seez, carried out the first detailed simulation studies of the most plausible way to detect the SM [[Higgs boson]] in the low-mass region in the environment of the [[Large Hadron Collider|LHC]]: via its decay into two photons.<ref name="Photon decay modes of the intermediate mass Higgs">{{cite web|title=Photon decay modes of the intermediate mass Higgs|url=http://cdsweb.cern.ch/record/220524/files/p474.pdf}}</ref> After intensive R&D Virdee argued that dense scintillating crystals offer the best possibility of achieving excellent energy resolution. In 1994, he made a compelling case for the use of lead tungstate scintillating crystals (PbWO<sub>4</sub>) for the electromagnetic calorimeter of [[Compact Muon Solenoid|CMS]]<ref name="A Crystal calorimeter for CMS at LHC">{{Cite book |chapter=A Crystal calorimeter for CMS at LHC|title=4th International Conference on Calorimetry in High-energy Physics|pages=347–356|chapter-url=http://inspirehep.net/record/364411|access-date=7 December 2012|year=1993|last1=Virdee|first1=T. S.}}</ref> as being the most promising detector for the discovery of the Higgs boson via its two-photon decay mode. He made the case within the CMS experiment, to CERN’s Management and to the LHCC. He led the team that proved the viability of this technique,<ref name="Studies of Lead Tungstate Crystal Matrices in High Energy Beams for the CMS Electromagnetic Calorimeter at the LHC">{{cite web|title=Studies of Lead Tungstate Crystal Matrices in High Energy Beams for the CMS Electromagnetic Calorimeter at the LHC|url=http://cdsweb.cern.ch/record/314616/files/ppe-96-148.pdf}}</ref> a technique that has played a crucial role in the discovery of the new heavy boson,<ref name="Observation of a new boson at a mass of 125 GeV with the CMS experiment at the LHC">{{Cite journal|title=Observation of a new boson at a mass of 125 GeV with the CMS experiment at the LHC|journal=Physics Letters B|volume=716|issue=2012|pages=30|arxiv=1207.7235|author1= The CMS Collaboration|year=2012|doi=10.1016/j.physletb.2012.08.021|last2=Khachatryan|first2=V.|last3=Sirunyan|first3=A.M.|last4=Tumasyan|first4=A.|last5=Adam|first5=W.|last6=Aguilo|first6=E.|last7=Bergauer|first7=T.|last8=Dragicevic|first8=M.|last9=Erö|first9=J.|last10=Fabjan|first10=C.|last11=Friedl|first11=M.|last12=Frühwirth|first12=R.|last13=Ghete|first13=V.M.|last14=Hammer|first14=J.|last15=Hoch|first15=M.|last16=Hörmann|first16=N.|last17=Hrubec|first17=J.|last18=Jeitler|first18=M.|last19=Kiesenhofer|first19=W.|last20=Knünz|first20=V.|last21=Krammer|first21=M.|last22=Krätschmer|first22=I.|last23=Liko|first23=D.|last24=Majerotto|first24=W.|last25=Mikulec|first25=I.|last26=Pernicka|first26=M.|last27=Rahbaran|first27=B.|last28=Rohringer|first28=C.|last29=Rohringer|first29=H.|last30=Schöfbeck|first30=R.|display-authors=29|bibcode=2012PhLB..716...30C}}</ref><ref name="Journey in the Search for the Higgs Boson: The ATLAS and CMS Experiments at the Large Hadron Collider">{{cite journal|last=Della Negra|first=M.|author2=Jenni, P. |author3=Virdee, T. S. |title=Journey in the Search for the Higgs Boson: The ATLAS and CMS Experiments at the Large Hadron Collider|journal=Science|date=20 December 2012|volume=338|issue=6114|pages=1560–1568|doi=10.1126/science.1230827|pmid=23258886|bibcode=2012Sci...338.1560D|doi-access=}}</ref> in July 2012. Virdee was deeply involved in the data analysis for the search for the Higgs boson, especially via its two-photon decay mode whose analysis was very much along the lines described in the study above. CMS’ signal for the discovery of the Higgs boson was the strongest in this decay mode.

Virdee was the deputy project leader of [[Compact Muon Solenoid|CMS]] between 1993 and 2006 and was then elected project leader (Spokesperson) in January 2007 for a period of three years.<ref name="Elected Spokesperson">{{Cite journal|title=Elected Spokesperson for 3 years|journal=CERN Bulletin|url=http://cdsweb.cern.ch/record/967461|year=2006}}</ref> He oversaw the final stages of construction, installation and data taking with the first collisions at the [[Large Hadron Collider|LHC]].

Virdee is a major voice in arguing for the long-term future of the [[Large Hadron Collider|LHC]] accelerator and its experiments. An increase in the interaction rate by almost a factor of around ten is being advocated for the CMS and [[ATLAS experiment|ATLAS]] experiments.<ref name="Physics potential and experimental challenges of the LHC luminosity upgrade">{{cite journal|last=Gianotti|first=F.|author2=Mangano, M. L. |author3=Virdee, T. |title=Physics potential and experimental challenges of the LHC luminosity upgrade|journal=The European Physical Journal C|year=2005|volume=39|issue=3|pages=293–333|doi=10.1140/epjc/s2004-02061-6|bibcode=2005EPJC...39..293G|arxiv=hep-ph/0204087|s2cid=3498118|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/546399}}</ref> To benefit fully from this luminosity increase the CMS detector will be upgraded. Virdee is leading efforts to replace the detector's endcaps with a novel silicon-based technology that measures the energy and momentum of particles to unprecedented levels of precision.<ref>{{cite web|title=Exploring the Terascale at LHC with Novel Highly Granular Calorimeters|url=https://erc.europa.eu/projects-figures/erc-funded-projects/results?search_api_views_fulltext=&page=78&items_per_page=20&f&#91;0&#93;=funding_scheme%3AAdvanced%20Grant%20%28AdG%29|website=European Research Council|access-date=2 April 2018|archive-date=7 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200807231029/https://erc.europa.eu/projects-figures/erc-funded-projects/results?search_api_views_fulltext=&page=78&items_per_page=20&f%5B0%5D=funding_scheme%3AAdvanced%20Grant%20%28AdG%29|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Beyond his contributions to particle physics he is a promoter of science and education, especially in Africa.<ref name="CERN and Science in Africa">{{cite web|title=CERN and Science in Africa|url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/podcasts/series/discovery/all#playepisode38|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110109091134/http://www.bbc.co.uk/podcasts/series/discovery/all#playepisode38|url-status=dead|archive-date=9 January 2011|access-date=17 May 2014}}</ref><ref name="IOPAfrica">{{cite web|title=Applications invited for Africa projects grant scheme|url=http://www.iop.org/news/16/feb/page_66992.html|website=Institute of Physics|access-date=20 August 2016}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> He funds science-related education activities in schools and universities in Africa, India and the United Kingdom.<ref>{{cite web |title=Support and grants |url=http://www.iop.org/about/grants/ |website=IOP Institute of Physics |access-date=6 June 2019 }}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=IOP Institute of Physics Blog |url=http://www.iopblog.org/bringing-science-to-the-public-in-nairobi/ |access-date=6 June 2019 |publisher=IOP |date=15 March 2018}}</ref>

==Invited lectures and outreach==
Virdee has given several keynote speeches at international conferences, opening or closing addresses at particle physics conferences and public lectures on the LHC Project.
These include the 2007 Schrödinger Lecture,<ref name="2007 Schrödinger Lecture">{{cite web|title=2007 Schrödinger Lecture|url=http://www3.imperial.ac.uk/events/theschrodingerlecture|access-date=10 December 2012}}</ref> the 2012 Peter Lindsay Lectures at Imperial College,<ref name="2012 Peter Lindsay Memorial Lecture">{{cite web|title=2012 Peter Lindsay Memorial Lecture|url=http://www3.imperial.ac.uk/newsandeventspggrp/imperialcollege/eventssummary/event_1-3-2012-15-0-10|access-date=10 December 2012}}</ref> the 16th Kaczmarczik Lecture at Drexel University,<ref name="16th Annual Kaczmarczik Lecture">{{cite web|title=16th Annual Kaczmarczik Lecture|url=http://drexel.edu/coas/news/archive/20110408/|access-date=10 December 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130119191136/http://www.drexel.edu/coas/news/archive/20110408/|archive-date=19 January 2013}}</ref> Philadelphia in 2011, the Keynote Speech at the 2009 Intel International Science and Engineering Fair, Reno, USA<ref name="2009 Intel International Science and Engineering Fair">{{cite web|title=2009 Intel International Science and Engineering Fair|url=http://www.societyforscience.org/Document.Doc?id=8|access-date=10 December 2012}}</ref> and joint lectures on the LHC Project with Prof. [[Edward Witten]] in Philadelphia, U.S.A. (2008)<ref name="2008 Joint Lectures: Virdee and Witten">{{cite web|title=2008 Joint Lectures: Virdee and Witten|url=http://ichep08.com/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=14&Itemid=102}}</ref> and Split, Croatia (2009).

Amongst his interviews are a dialogue with [[A. C. Grayling]],<ref name="A.C. Grayling: Exchanges At The Frontier 2009">{{cite web|title=A.C. Grayling: Exchanges At The Frontier 2009|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/p005fbrf|access-date=10 December 2012}}</ref> and an interview with [[Jim Al-Khalili]] on the [[BBC]] Radio 4 programme “The Life Scientific”.<ref name="BBC World Service: Life Scientific"/>

* 2012 “''Searching for the Higgs boson''”, Cheltenham Science Festival, U.K.<ref name="Cheltenham Science Festival">{{cite web|title=Cheltenham Science Festival Brochure 2012, Page 17|work=Issuu |date=21 March 2012 |url=http://issuu.com/cheltenhamfestivals/docs/cf_science_festival_brochure|access-date=17 May 2014}}</ref>
* 2011 “''Exploring Nature Moments after the Big Bang: The LHC Accelerator and the CMS Experiment''”, 16th Kaczmarczik Lecture, Drexel University, Philadelphia, U.S.A.<ref name="16th Annual Kaczmarczik Lecture"/>
* 2009 “''Discovering the Quantum Universe; The LHC Project at CERN''”, Keynote Speaker at the Intel Science and Engineering Fair in Reno, U.S.A.<ref name="Intel ISEF">{{cite web|title=CERN welcomes 13 Intel ISEF pre-college winners|url=http://cerncourier.com/cws/article/cnl/40381|publisher=CERN|access-date=17 May 2014}}</ref> ([https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=071f_tU_nzQ video])

* 2007 “''Discovering the Quantum Universe: The Large Hadron Collider Project at CERN''”, 20th Schrodinger Lecture, Centennial of Imperial College: London, U.K.<ref name="2007 Schrödinger Lecture"/> ([http://www.imperial.ac.uk/podcasts/Schrodinger2007.m4v video])
